On April 24, 1964 at approximately 17:45, Socorro Police radio dispatcher Nep Lopez received a radio call from Sergeant Lonnie Zamora reporting a possible motor vehicle accident.

claims.v: Zamora claimed he saw two people dressed in white beside a shiny egg shaped object that later rose into the air accompanied by a roaring blue and orange flame
claims.quote: The Lonnie Zamora incident was an alleged UFO sighting that occurred on April 24, 1964 near Socorro, New Mexico, when Socorro police officer Lonnie Zamora claimed that he saw two people dressed in white beside a shiny egg shaped object that later rose into the air accompanied by a roaring blue and orange flame.

claims.v: radio call reporting a possible motor vehicle accident
claims.quote: On April 24, 1964 at approximately 17:45, Socorro Police radio dispatcher Nep Lopez received a radio call from Sergeant Lonnie Zamora reporting a possible motor vehicle accident.

claims.v: news media and UFO investigators and organizations
claims.quote: Zamora's claims were subject to attention from news media and UFO investigators and organizations, and the U.S. Air Force's Project Blue Book listed the case as "unknown".

claims.v: unknown

claims.v: burning brush examined by Chavez
claims.quote: When Chavez arrived, he asked Zamora what the trouble was. Zamora led him to examine some burning brush.

claims.v: patches of smoldering grass and brush noted by other police officers
claims.quote: When other police officers arrived, they noted patches of smoldering grass and brush.

claims.v: shallow holes in the ground, which Zamora said was from the object landing
claims.quote: There were also shallow holes in the ground, which Zamora said was from the object landing.

claims.v: south of Socorro, New Mexico
claims.quote: Zamora told authorities he was pursuing a speeding car south of Socorro, New Mexico, when he "heard a roar and saw a flame in the sky to southwest some distance away", which he approximated as being between a half mile to a mile away (0.80–1.61 km).

claims.v: arroyo below a mesa top
claims.quote: Consequently, stone walkways and steps were built into the arroyo from the mesa top, with a rock walkway circling the supposed landing site that included  some wooden benches.

claims.v: lunar lander test by White Sands Missile Range
claims.quote: Conventional explanations of Zamora's claims include a lunar lander test by White Sands Missile Range and a hoax by New Mexico Tech students.

claims.v: hoax by New Mexico Tech students
claims.quote: Conventional explanations of Zamora's claims include a lunar lander test by White Sands Missile Range and a hoax by New Mexico Tech students.

claims.v: mirage of the star Canopus
claims.quote: UFO skeptic Steuart Campbell has suggested that everything seen and heard by Zamora and fellow witnesses was "almost certainly" a mirage of the star Canopus.

claims.v: plan by the municipal government to increase tourism
claims.quote: Skeptic Philip J. Klass, who visited Socorro several years after the incident, claimed that the entire event was part of a plan by the municipal government to increase tourism.
